_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Mathematical Literacy P2, November 2018 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Mathematical
Literacy questions hang off shared scenario boxes: the scenario (tables, graphs, plans and maps
described in bracketed words) is the 'context' of the first sub-question of each block and applies
to the sub-questions after it. memo_answer gives the guideline's working and final answer with
decimal commas kept; the guideline's mark codes (M method, A accuracy, CA consistent accuracy, RT
reading from table, C conclusion, O opinion, S simplification, R rounding) and level tags are left out.
FORMAT: 75 marks, 1½ hours, four compulsory questions (Q1 25, Q2 20, Q3 18, Q4 12). An official
ERRATA sheet issued after the paper is tracked as paper2_errata.pdf: the conversion printed in 2.2
(1 cm³ = 1 000 litres) is incorrect, so Question 2 was to be marked out of 14 and scaled up to 20;
this is recorded in memo_note on 2.2.

subject: Mathematical Literacy

questions.context: QUESTION 1 | 1.1 Duanita works as an editor for 'The Correct Language Company'. She receives a basic salary every month. The number on the salary slip indicates the number of months she has been working for the company. Below is a copy of Duanita's salary slip for February 2018. [SALARY SLIP. Employee name: Duanita Verwey; identity number: 8903305432083; marital status: single; tax reference no.: 987234560; bank account no.: 24681XXXX; salary slip no.: 75; pay date: 25 February 2018. Earnings: basic salary (B); gross salary (B). Deductions: tax R2 923,25; UIF R224,00; medical aid R1 182,00; pension R1 875,00; total deductions (A). Net salary R18 795,75.] Use the above salary slip to answer the questions below.
questions.text: Determine the missing values of A and B respectively.
Show with the necessary calculations that the deduction for Pension is 7,5%.
questions.memo_answer: % pension deduction = 1 875 ÷ 25 000 x 100% = 7,5%

questions.text: Determine the number of years and months that Duanita has been working for this company.
questions.memo_answer:
Payslip no. 75: years = 75 ÷ 12 = 6,25 years
Months = 0,25 x 12 = 3 months
6 years and 3 months

questions.text: Why do you think some of the digits have been omitted from the account number?
questions.memo_answer: Privacy OR confidentiality OR to prevent fraud

questions.text: Duanita is offered an increase of 6,4%. She claims that her net pay for March will be R1 000 more than the net pay for February. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether her statement is valid or not. NOTE: Her tax will increase by R175,00, the pension will increase by R120,00 and the medical aid and UIF will remain unchanged.
questions.memo_answer:
New salary = R25 000 x 1,064 = R26 600
New tax = R2 923,25 + R175,00 = R3 098,25
New pension = R1 875,00 + R120,00 = R1 995
Net pay = R26 600 - (R3 098,25 + R1 995 + R224,00 + R1 182,00) = R26 600 - R6 499,25 = R20 100,75
Difference in net pay = R20 100,75 - R18 795,75 = R1 305,00
Statement valid (no mark for opinion without calculations).

questions.context: 1.2 Duanita wants a garden box at the back of her house to plant some herbs. She decides to buy the garden box below. [Diagram: a rectangular box 100 cm long, 35 cm wide and 70 cm high.]
questions.text: Calculate the area of the base of the garden box. Give your final answer in square metres (m2). You may use the following formula: Area = length x breadth
questions.memo_answer: Area of base = length x breadth = 100 cm x 35 cm = 1 m x 0,35 m = 0,35 m² (penalise an incorrect unit)

questions.text: The garden box cannot be filled with sand right to the top. The garden box can only be filled to 75% of its height. Calculate the height of the sand in the garden box to the nearest centimetre.
questions.memo_answer: Height of sand = 0,75 x 70 cm = 52,5 cm ≈ 53 cm

questions.context: QUESTION 2 | 2.1 Water has become a critical issue in South Africa, especially in the Western Cape and the Eastern Cape, where dam levels have dropped tremendously over the past few years. Below is a table showing the major supply dams in the Western Cape. [TABLE 1: WATER STORAGE IN THE MAJOR DAMS COMPRISING THE WESTERN CAPE WATER SUPPLY SYSTEM. Columns: Major dam | Capacity (Mℓ) | % storage on 25 June 2018 | 2017 | 2016 | 2015 | 2014. Berg River 130 010 | 67,8 | 36,5 | 38,7 | 60,0 | 100,2; Steenbras Lower 33 517 | 46,5 | 30,2 | 37,1 | 55,4 | 72,6; Steenbras Upper 31 767 | 96,5 | 60,6 | 65,8 | 57,4 | 101,3; Theewaterskloof 480 188 | 30,4 | 18,6 | 33,9 | 54,9 | 98,5; Voëlvlei 164 095 | 37,6 | 18,4 | 27,4 | 39,2 | 81,6; Wemmershoek 58 644 | 71,2 | 37,5 | 50,1 | 53,2 | 89,8. Total stored (Mℓ) 898 221 (capacity) | 383 263 | 218 433 | 320 741 | 474 301 | 846 413. % storage: A | 24,3 | 35,7 | 52,8 | 94,2.] *The last 10% of a dam's water is difficult to use, so the usable water in the dam is approximately 10% less than the dam level. Use TABLE 1 above to answer the questions below.
questions.text: Determine the value of A (the percentage storage for 25 June 2018).
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_note: The guideline writes 383 203; the table total is 383 263, which also gives 42,7%.

questions.text: Describe a possible trend for the period in terms of the total water stored.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_answer: From 2014 to 2017 the water storage decreased and then increased in 2018.

questions.text: Give ONE possible reason for the low dam levels from 2015 to 2017.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_answer: Below-average rainfall OR low rainfall

questions.text: Calculate the mean percentage of the dams in 2016.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_note: The six 2016 values add to 253,0, not 250, so the mean is 253 ÷ 6 = 42,2% (42,17%); the guideline prints 250 and 41,7%.

questions.text: Calculate the probability that a dam will have 45% or more water stored on 25 June 2018. Write your final answer to 3 decimal places.
questions.memo_answer: Probability = 4/6 = 0,667

questions.text: Mervyn bought a water tank to store water. Study the diagram of the water tank below and answer the questions that follow. [Picture of a cylindrical water tank.] The water tank has the following dimensions: diameter = 1 500 mm; height = 1 820 mm. You may use the following formula and conversion: Volume = π x radius x radius x height, where π = 3,142. Conversion: 1 cm³ = 1 000 litres. The capacity of the water tank is advertised as 3 000 litres. Hence, calculate the capacity of the water tank by using the dimensions and account for the difference between the advertised capacity and the capacity that you have calculated.
questions.memo_answer:
Volume = π x radius x radius x height = 3,142 x 750 mm x 750 mm x 1 820 mm = 3,142 x 75 cm x 75 cm x 182 cm = 3 216 622,5 cm³ = 3 216,6225 litres
The advertised capacity refers to the maximum amount of water the tank can hold, while the calculated capacity refers to the actual content of the tank. (Accept any other relevant explanation.)
questions.memo_note: The conversion printed in the question (1 cm³ = 1 000 litres) is wrong: 1 000 cm³ = 1 litre, which the guideline uses. The official errata (13 Nov 2018) says Question 2 is to be marked out of 14 and scaled up to 20.

questions.context: QUESTION 3 | 3.1 Jona buys a sand pit for his 4-year-old daughter, Jaimee, and puts it in his backyard. Below is a diagram of the sandpit with dimensions. [Photograph of a square wooden sandpit labelled 190 cm and 160 cm along the base edges, 31 cm high, with a 19,5 cm wide bench seat along one side.]
questions.text: Jona finds a space to put the sandpit, but he only considers the perimeter of the base of the sand pit. Calculate the perimeter of the base of the sand pit. Give your final answer in metres. You may use the following formula: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × breadth
questions.memo_answer: Perimeter of base = 2 x length + 2 x breadth = (2 x 190 cm) + (2 x 160 cm) = (2 x 1,9 m) + (2 x 1,6 m) = 3,8 m + 3,2 m = 7 m

questions.text: The sand that Jona wants to put in the sand pit, should only cover 80,5% of the height of the sandpit. Determine the height of the sand in the sand pit to the nearest centimetre.
questions.memo_answer: Height of the sand = 0,805 x 31 cm = 24,955 cm ≈ 25 cm

questions.context: 3.2 Jona's daughter Jaimee attends a playschool. The following is a floor plan of the playschool. [Floor plan: JELLY BABIES 3 months to 1 year room, sleep room and changing room on the left; JELLY BABIES 1 to 2 years room next to them; staffroom, kitchen, laundry, disabled toilets, sports hall and toilets along the top; store, office, entrance lobby and library in the middle; JELLY TOTS 2 to 3 years playroom and JELLY BEANS 3 to 5 years playroom on the right.]
questions.text: Joan’s neighbours also want to enrol their 6-year-old son at Jaimee’s playschool. Give evidence from the floorplan to show whether the playschool will accept the neighbour’s son.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale, floor plans and elevation plans
questions.memo_answer: The playschool only caters for children from 3 months to 5 years old, so the 6-year-old will not be accepted.

questions.text: Does this playschool cater for disabled children? Justify your answer with evidence from the floorplan.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale, floor plans and elevation plans
questions.memo_answer: Yes. There are toilets for the disabled.

questions.text: Give ONE possible reason why the 3 months to 1-year-old and 1-year to 2-year-old classrooms are situated far away from the 2-year to 5-year-old classrooms.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale, floor plans and elevation plans
questions.memo_answer: Safety reasons OR noise levels of crying babies OR close to the changing room (accept any other relevant explanation)

questions.context: 3.3 The playschool fees are structured as follows: [Age - fee per month: 3 months to 1 year and 6 months R1 050; 1 year and 7 months to 3 years and 6 months R820; 3 years and 7 months to 5 years R550.]
questions.text: Give ONE possible reason why the fees for 3 months to 1 year and 6 months are much higher than the others.
questions.memo_answer: The infants from 3 months to 1 year 6 months need more attention; they need to be changed regularly. (Accept any other relevant explanation.)

questions.text: The playschool hosts 35 children of which nine are in the age group 3 months to 1 year and 6 months, ten in the age group 1 year and 7 months to 3 years and 6 months and the rest in the age group 3 year and 7 months to 5 years. Calculate the playschool’s income for one year if none of the learners has withdrawn.

questions.context: QUESTION 4 | 4.1 Below is an extract from a map of Soweto. [Map of Soweto with a north arrow (N up) and a bar scale (0-1 000 metres): the N1 runs south from Johannesburg CBD on the east side of Soweto past the N12 interchange towards Bloemfontein; the N12 runs west from its junction with the N1, south of Soweto past Eldorado Park, towards Carltonville on the western edge; suburbs shown include Roodepoort, Robertsville, Meadowlands, Dobsonville, Orlando, Doornkop, Jabulani, Protea, Pimville, Devland, Lenasia and Naturena.]
questions.text: Describe the route that you must take, with geographical directions, if you have to travel from Johannesburg CBD to Carltonville.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale and maps
questions.memo_answer: Travel south on the N1, pass the off-ramp on the east, turn west at the intersection of the N1 and N12 and continue on the N12.

questions.text: Write the bar scale (line scale) as a unit scale.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale and maps
questions.memo_answer:
Bar scale: 1,8 cm = 1 000 m = 100 000 cm
1 cm = 55 555,55556 cm
Unit scale 1 : 55 555,55556 (accept a measurement of 1,7-1,9 cm; no mark for the final answer if units are given)

questions.text: In December 2017 the total number of tourists who visited Soweto was 1,5 million. This was an increase of 6,25% from December 2016. Calculate the number of tourists who visited Soweto in 2016.
Give ONE possible reason why more people visit Soweto in December than in any other month.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_answer: Holiday in December OR people have money to travel (accept any other relevant reason)
